name: Link
layerWhy: It keeps one part of a promise: it takes you somewhere. Moving is never a whole job.
promise: It takes the person to another place and changes nothing.
expectation: Following it goes somewhere; it says when that is away from this site or a file.
evidence: An address on another site opens in a new tab with an arrow shown and "(opens in a new tab)" read; a download shows an arrow down and the file's type and size.
behaviour: External addresses open in a new tab with rel="noopener noreferrer".
A download shows its file type and size when given.
Back always returns to where the person was.
context: In running text, in lists of places, and as a button-shaped link when it starts a task on its own page.
relationships: Its words name the destination, not "here".
A link that looks like a button still only navigates.
accessibility: The new-tab warning is read, not only shown.
The arrows are content with empty alternative text.
failures: Never opens a new tab without saying so.
dont: A link that deletes or saves.

inputs: external: opens elsewhere (another site by default)
file: what a download is ("PDF, 2 MB")

usage.markup: Download Report
